items.summary: English is one language with many accents, and most of the differences you meet are regular rather than wrong. After reading this you can recognise British, American, Australian, Indian and Singapore English by their vocabulary and grammar, understand why the differences exist, and choose the variety that fits your listener.
items.title: Why English Is Different Around the World

items.summary: A breakdown is a conversation you will have while standing on a hard shoulder, so the words matter. After reading this you can make the scene safe, describe the fault in a way that gets the right help sent, say what you need, and look after the people around you until someone arrives.
items.title: What to Say When Your Car Breaks Down

items.summary: A food label tells you three things: what is inside, how much of it there is, and how long it is safe. After reading this you can read any label in any country, tell a use-by date from a best-before date, and decide at the shelf whether a product is worth buying.
items.title: Reading Food Labels and Expiration Dates

items.summary: The nutrition panel is a set of numbers with a specific meaning, and the ingredient list is a set of names with a specific meaning. After reading this you can read any food label, judge a serving for yourself, compare two products fairly, check a claim on the front of the pack against the numbers behind it, and read a label with a specific medical need in mind.
items.title: Understanding Nutrition Facts and Food Ingredients

items.summary: Sleep is not lost time. It is when your body repairs, consolidates memory and regulates mood. After reading this you can judge whether you are actually getting enough, understand what your sleep cycle does, remove the habits that quietly break your nights, build a wind-down routine that fits a real week, and know when poor sleep needs a doctor.
items.title: Why Sleep Matters More Than You Think

items.summary: Nam finds his grandfather's old bicycle with two paper wings taped to the frame, and it flies over the rooftops of the old quarter. Follow him past the lake, the wind and the moment he thinks he is lost. After reading, you can retell the flight, use five new words about flying in your own sentences, and say why the bicycle needed a second pair of hands.
items.title: The Flying Bicycle Adventure

items.summary: Hà finds a castle that only appears to children who come with empty hands, and she spends one whole day inside it. Follow her through the kitchen, the library and the garden, and to the great door with the small slot. After reading, you can retell the day, use five new castle words in your own sentences, and explain what the castle gave back.
items.title: One Day in a Magical Castle

items.summary: Butterflies do not arrive in the world as butterflies. They start as eggs and change their whole shape. After reading this, you can name the four stages of a butterfly, tell a caterpillar from a chrysalis, and help a butterfly grow in your garden without hurting it.
items.title: How Butterflies Grow and Change

items.summary: Birds build nests for four good reasons, and every species has its own design. After reading this you can say what a nest is for, name the parts of an egg, recognise six kinds of nest, and watch birds without disturbing them.
items.title: Why Do Birds Build Nests?

items.summary: A pet is an animal that lives with you and depends on you every day. After reading this, you can tell what different pets need, feed and care for one properly, and know the safety rules that keep both you and the animal well.
items.title: Pets and How to Care for Them

items.summary: The savanna is a great open grassland full of grass eaters and hungry hunters. After reading this you can name the animals that live there, use the words scientists use for them, and explain what happens on a savanna in the space of one day.
items.title: Amazing Animals of the African Savanna

items.summary: Most children have an animal they love most. After reading this you can name your favourite animal, say where it lives and what it eats, and describe an animal so well that somebody else can picture it.
items.title: Talking About Your Favorite Animals

items.summary: Bedtime is a routine, and a routine is a set of small steps you repeat every night. After reading this you can get ready for bed in the right order, say the bedtime words, talk with your family before sleep, and calm down when you cannot fall asleep.
items.title: Getting Ready for Bedtime

items.summary: Asking for food is a skill you can learn. After reading this you can ask politely for a drink or a dish, order at a café or a shop, and say clearly when you cannot eat something.
items.title: Asking for Food and Drinks

items.summary: A friend at school is someone you meet, talk to, and play with again and again. After reading this you can say hello to a new child, join a game, find something you both like, and keep a new friendship going.
items.title: Making Friends at School

items.summary: A good question is a small key that opens a big door. After reading this you can ask a clear question in class, use the right question words, wait for your turn, and ask a teacher or grown-up for help politely.
items.title: Asking Questions in the Classroom

items.summary: Anger is a big feeling that comes fast and goes slow. After reading this, you can name what makes you angry, know where you feel it in your body, calm yourself in five steps, and choose words that do not hurt people.
items.title: What to Do When You Feel Angry

items.summary: Sharing feels hard at first, and it gets easier with practice. After reading this, you can name the feeling, ask for a turn in words, wait your turn calmly, and keep a toy that is truly yours.
items.title: Learning to Share and Take Turns

items.summary: Please and thank you are two small words that make people happy. After reading this you can ask for things politely, say thank you at the right moment, and help other people feel good too.
items.title: Learning to Say Please and Thank You

items.summary: A feeling is a message from inside you. After reading this you can name what you feel, say it out loud to a grown-up or a friend, and help a friend who is feeling sad.
items.title: How Do You Feel Today?

items.summary: A fruit is a plant part that holds seeds. After reading this you can name the parts of a fruit, tell your friends where your fruit comes from, and wash and cut fruit safely at home.
items.title: Let's Learn About Fruits

items.summary: Milk starts on a farm, inside a cow. After reading this you can tell your family where milk comes from, name the parts of a dairy, and choose a kind of milk at the shop.
items.title: Where Does Milk Come From?

items.summary: A snack is small food between meals. After reading this you can tell a snack from a meal, build a balanced snack plate, choose snacks that keep you full, and ask politely for one at school.
items.title: Healthy Snacks for Happy Kids

items.summary: Vegetables are the colourful parts of plants that we eat. After reading this you can name vegetables by their colours, say where they grow, and help prepare a simple dish at home.
items.title: Vegetables and Their Colors

items.summary: The bathroom holds the things that keep us clean and well. After reading this, you can name the things in a bathroom, wash your hands the right way, and stay safe near water, hot water and sharp things.
items.title: Things We Use in the Bathroom

items.summary: Your bedroom is your own little world. After reading this, you can name the things in a bedroom, say what each one is for, and keep your room clean and happy on your own.
items.title: What's Inside My Bedroom?

items.summary: Your school bag carries your day with you. After reading this, you can name what is inside, pack it the night before, and take care of your things so they last.
items.title: My School Bag and What's Inside

items.summary: Everything around you has a shape and a colour. After reading this, you can name the common shapes and colours, find them in your home and your street, and use them to draw and build your own pictures.
items.title: Learning About Shapes and Colors

items.summary: A toy is something we play with, and every toy has a way to play with it. After reading this, you can name the toys around you, choose the right game for each toy, play well with friends, and keep your toys in good shape.
items.title: Toys and How We Play With Them

items.summary: An airplane is heavy, and yet it flies. After reading this, you can explain why the wings hold a plane up, name the parts of an airplane, and tell what happens between the airport gate and the sky.
items.title: How Do Airplanes Fly?

items.summary: Every plant starts small and builds itself one part at a time. A seed wakes up, sends down a root, pushes up a shoot, opens leaves and makes its own food from light, water and air. After reading this you can grow a seed and watch each part appear, name the parts of a plant, and explain how a plant makes its food.
items.title: How Do Plants Grow?

items.summary: Rain is old water that has taken a long trip. Water from rivers, lakes and puddles rises into the air, cools, gathers into clouds, and falls back down as drops. After reading this you can explain where rain comes from, name the three steps of the water cycle, and tell the difference between rain, drizzle, snow and hail.
items.title: Where Does Rain Come From?

items.summary: The sky is full of lights, but they are not all the same kind of thing. After reading this, you can say what the Sun, the Moon and a star each are, explain why the Moon seems to change shape, and find real stars in the night sky without a telescope.
items.title: The Sun, the Moon, and the Stars

items.summary: Brushing feels normal, but teeth are in real danger every single day. After reading this, you can explain what plaque does to a tooth, brush properly, and pick snacks that are kinder to your teeth.
items.title: Why Do We Brush Our Teeth?

items.summary: A bear keeps every pot of honey for himself, and says no to all his friends. Follow him through autumn into the cold winter, when his friends share with him instead. After reading, you can retell the story, use its new words, and tell its lesson about sharing.
items.title: The Bear Who Learned to Share

items.summary: Wren watches the other birds fly and wants to fly too, but she is afraid of falling. Follow her from the branch to the sky. You will learn the three parts of the story, four new words, and the small step that helped her leave the nest.
items.title: The Little Bird Who Wanted to Fly

items.summary: Pip slips out of the gate and loses his way in the rain. Follow him from the first wet paw to the last step home. You will learn the three parts of a story, the words Pip's story uses, and the little trick that helped him find his own front door.
items.title: The Lost Puppy Finds His Way Home

items.summary: Pip is a little rabbit who cannot sleep because the night is dark. Follow Pip from the burrow to the woods, where a lamp goes out and something wonderful appears. After reading this story you can tell it back to someone, name the words inside it, and share the small lesson it carries.
items.title: The Little Rabbit Who Was Afraid of the Dark

items.summary: An always tells the truth, even when the truth is hard to say. Follow him through the day he breaks his mother's blue bowl. You will learn the three parts of the story, four new words, and what happened when he chose not to hide.
items.title: The Boy Who Always Told the Truth

items.summary: A credit card is a loan with a billing cycle attached. After reading this you can work out what a balance really costs, why the minimum payment takes years to clear, which card traps cost the most, and what to say when you call your bank.
items.title: Understanding Credit Cards and Interest Rates
